title: Prior-only persistence weighting of Q93 leading pair-residual spectral subspaces

target_design.cutoff_rule: For target i, compute the current pair-residual eigenspace from draws[:i] only. Compare it with the preceding target's prior-only eigenspace. Read the target quintet only after all rankings for that target are frozen.

hypothesis: Q93's leading k=2 spectral operator retains about 72% of pair-residual energy but does not improve ranking consistently. Its failure may be due to rapidly rotating or unstable leading eigenspaces. Weighting the spectral ranking contribution by prior-only subspace persistence may suppress unstable spectral noise and improve out-of-sample ranking.

spectral_persistence.pair_residual: For target i, E_pair_i is q90.decompose_edge_change(E_i-E_(i-1)).pair, with E_i computed from draws[:i].
spectral_persistence.leading_subspace: Use q93.spectral_modes(E_pair_i, 2), including the complete absolute-eigenvalue tie group under Q93's fixed 1e-10 cutoff tolerance.
spectral_persistence.overlap: For current and previous orthonormal bases V_i and V_(i-1), stability_i = ||V_i.T @ V_(i-1)||_F^2 / min(r_i,r_(i-1)); if either subspace is empty, stability_i=0. Clip numerical roundoff to [0,1].
spectral_persistence.interpretation: For equal dimensions this is the mean squared cosine of principal angles. For unequal tie-expanded dimensions it is the normalized overlap of the smaller subspace with the larger one.
spectral_persistence.rank_rule: Convert scores to a deterministic 1..40 ranking with q87.field.rank_from_scores; ties follow the existing engine's deterministic rule.

frozen_parameters.rank_blend: convex ordinal-rank blend; no fitted coefficient

statistics.exact_null: 45 tests: 5 named models x 3 chronological splits x Top5/Top10/Top20; exact Hypergeometric(40,k,5) upper-tail null; one global Holm family.
statistics.paired: 24 tests: Validation and historical Blind OOS x 4 comparators (Equal42, Q90 pair interaction, Q93 k=2, Q94 instability control) x Top5/Top10/Top20; circular moving-block bootstrap length 20, 2,000 replicates; one global Holm family.
statistics.circular_shift: 99 fixed nonzero circular shifts of the stability sequence within each split, seed 9401. This is a post-hoc alignment null only, never a forecast input. Compare focal Q94 stability-weighted mean hits against the 99 shifted-weight means for each split and endpoint; plus-one p-values and one global Holm family of 9 tests.
statistics.primary_gate: On historical Blind OOS, Q94::STABILITY_WEIGHTED must exceed Q90::PAIR_INTERACTION_TRANSFER, BASE::EQUAL42 and Q93::SPECTRAL_K2 by at least 0.10 Top20 hits/target; each paired moving-block bootstrap 95% CI lower bound must be >0 and Holm p<0.05; focal exact-null Holm p<0.05; focal circular-shift randomization Holm p<0.05. Historical Blind OOS is exploratory, not prospective confirmation.

safeguards: Verify Q93 accepted manifest, validation and source-ledger SHA-256 before using its frozen prior-only rankings.
Recompute every current and previous spectral subspace using strict prefixes draws[:i]; no target or future draw enters the graph, eigenspace, overlap, score or ranking.
The Q93 equal42 and k2 rankings are consumed only as pre-target ranking vectors; their outcomes are never used to calculate the current stability weight.
No coefficient, mode count, threshold or model is tuned on Validation or historical Blind OOS.
The circular-shift null is inferential only and is never used as a predictive model.
One global Holm family for exact-null tests, one for paired bootstrap tests and one for circular-shift randomization tests.
Moving-block bootstrap is reported separately because exact hypergeometric tests assume independent target draws.
Historical Blind OOS has been exposed in prior SONAR work and is exploratory, not virgin holdout.
The co-occurrence graph is a statistical descriptor, not physical coupling or proof of causality.
No immutable freeze modification, no prospective shadow insertion, no model promotion and no automatic merge.
known_limitations: Subspace overlap measures persistence of the leading spectral subspace, not causal transfer.
Ordinal-rank blending discards score magnitudes and is a deliberately simple, fixed diagnostic operator.
A high subspace overlap may be common under the structural constraints of zero-row-sum symmetric matrices; the circular-shift null tests temporal alignment, not all possible graph nulls.
Q60 prospective promotion still requires at least 200 complete paired targets; the latest registered count is 21.
